2024 Annual Town Meeting held May 6-7, 2024 at Acton-Boxborough Regional High School; 2,579 residents participated May 6. Article 12 passed 69% in favor, 31% opposed; Planning Board voted unanimously to recommend. Three new overlay districts created. MBTA Communities Act permits majority threshold rather than standard 2/3 zoning amendment threshold. EOHLC certified September 30, 2024. Seed extracted_planning_board entry 'recommended; art 12' confirmed.

City Council approved Council Bill 2024-098 on October 8, 2024, amending zoning ordinance to create Rocky Hill Multi-Family Overlay District (plus two pre-existing Smart Growth overlays). Planning Board June 10, 2024 meeting referenced in minutes as favorable; exact tally not retrievable (PDF). Vote tally not found in accessible sources. Seed adoption_date 2024-09-05 predates the Oct 8 council vote — likely reflects an interim/conditional EOHLC determination or earlier phased submission; discrepancy flagged.

MBTA zoning was placed in a Special Town Meeting (STM) held the second night of the ATM on April 30, 2024. The STM Article 1 passed by simple majority (434-196, 7 abstaining) -- the MBTA Communities Act (G.L. c.40A §3A) allows adoption by simple majority rather than the usual 2/3 zoning supermajority. Planning Board recommended approval (listed in ATM minutes). EOHLC certified compliance on 2024-09-13.

Arlington uses Representative Town Meeting (252 elected members). The MBTA Communities Overlay District was Article 12 at a Special Town Meeting (Session 4) on October 25, 2023. Passed 189-35. The Arlington Redevelopment Board (ARB) -- which serves as the planning authority in Arlington -- voted on October 2, 2023 to approve and recommend the article for town meeting. EOHLC certified November 8, 2023; AG approved June 2024.

MBTA zoning adopted at Special Town Meeting on October 27, 2025 as Article 2 (voice vote, declared passed by majority). Planning Board, Bylaw Review Committee, and Economic Development Committee all voted to support; Select Board and Advisory Board also recommended. The seed adoption_date of 2025-07-24 appears erroneous -- it predates both the August 27, 2025 Village Center MBTA presentation and the October 27, 2025 town meeting vote. EOHLC certification date is not yet independently confirmed but Compliant status is consistent with post-meeting certification. Passage by simple majority is consistent with G.L. c.40A §3A exception.

MBTA Communities Overlay District Bylaw approved at October 28, 2024 Special Town Meeting. Planning Board held public hearing September 10–24, 2024, voted 4-1 to recommend. Seed adoption_date of 2024-08-26 likely reflects EOHLC interim compliance acknowledgment predating the actual legislative vote; decisive legislative vote was October 28, 2024. Article number not recoverable from available public documents (warrant PDF binary-only).

MBTA multifamily zoning text (Article 11) and map (Article 12) both passed by overwhelming majority in a hand vote at the March 25, 2024 Annual Town Meeting; no numeric tally reported. Planning Board held public hearing February 13 and February 27, 2024, and voted to recommend both articles favorably; Planning Board itself sponsored the articles. AG approved the zoning in early July 2024. EOHLC certified compliance April 2025 — hence no EOHLC adoption_date in the seed. Adoption date in structured output is approximate (AG filing / effective date); seed field left blank.

Fall Town Meeting held November 20, 2024; CHAPA counted Bellingham among compliant communities approximately November 22, 2024, confirming adoption. MBTA Communities Overlay District (Article XXX in the town's zoning code) covers North Main Street and Mechanic Street subdistricts; map dated September 23, 2024 on file with Town Clerk. Warrant article number and numeric vote tally not recoverable from public search results. Planning board recommendation not confirmed in available sources. EOHLC certified December 9, 2024.

Special Town Meeting Nov 18-20, 2024 at Belmont High School. Article 2 (main 3A zoning district, simple majority threshold) adopted 213-8 on the final night (Nov 20). Planning Board voted 3-2 in favor of Map 1 (without Purecoat site) and endorsed either map as preferable to non-compliance. Companion Articles 3 (Inclusionary Housing) and 4 (Design/Site Plan Review) required 2/3. EOHLC final compliance confirmed spring 2025 after AG approval April 2025; seed adoption_date is blank (EOHLC has not yet recorded a district adoption date in the seed).

Special Town Meeting Nov 15, 2025; 212 attendees. Article 4 created Residential Development Overlay District (RDOD) along County Street (10 acres, up to 151 multifamily units) to comply with MBTA Communities Act (simple majority required). Planning Board Chairman Marc Oliveira confirmed PB voted unanimously (4-0 at Nov 12 public hearing) to recommend passage. Motion to postpone Article 4 was defeated before the main vote, which then carried unanimously. Seed EOHLC adoption_date of 2025-10-09 predates the town vote; likely reflects an earlier EOHLC pre-approval or interim action date rather than the district adoption date.

Beverly City Council adopted MBTA Communities 3A zoning amendments on November 12, 2024. Joint public hearing with City Council was held October 7, 2024; Planning Board closed its hearing and voted 6-0 favorable on October 8, 2024. Vote passed with little objection as Beverly was already substantially in compliance. No order number or council vote tally found in public records. EOHLC confirmed compliance April 2025 (Beverly's official page states compliance confirmed April 2025 following Dec 31, 2024 application submission). Seed adoption_date is blank.

Special Fall Town Meeting December 12, 2024. Article 1 created MBTA Communities Multi-Family Overlay District (MCMOD) with four subdistricts (Outer Mills, Inner Mills, Federal Street, Kenmar). Vote 94-46 confirmed by MHP Executive Director Jennifer Raitt via social media. Planning Board prepared and released final bylaw draft on 11/20/2024 and held open forum 12/2/2024; formal PB vote tally not publicly reported. EOHLC certified compliance 2024-12-18.

Special Town Meeting October 20, 2025. Article 12 passed 69-47 with heavy debate; approximately half of ~225 attendees abstained. Planning Board created the Multifamily Overlay District (MFOD) in the Downtown District of Buzzards Bay; formal PB vote tally/date not publicly confirmed. EOHLC seed adoption_date 2025-08-19 appears to reflect an interim compliance milestone predating the town meeting vote; final EOHLC compliance confirmation followed the October 2025 vote. Bourne is the only Cape Cod town subject to the MBTA Communities Act.

Fall Town Meeting October 14-15, 2025 (Boxboro Regency, 412 voters present). Article 6 created MBTA Communities Overlay District; passed 193-87, exceeding 2/3 threshold (~187 required). Planning Board voted 5-0 on September 3, 2025 to recommend adoption. Housing Board also voted unanimously in support August 27, 2025. EOHLC placed town in 'interim compliance' December 10, 2025 because the adopted bylaw's net density calculation was later found to overstate units per acre; town is correcting the error and is not facing penalties. Seed status Interim/Unknown is confirmed. No EOHLC-certified adoption date yet.

Planning Board voted 4-1 favorable under protest; chair Gore cast dissenting vote on principle. STM held Dec 17 2025 at Masconomet auditorium; motion to end debate passed 473-142 before all speakers heard. Prior attempt at Bradford Street district rejected by EOHLC in June 2025 (parcels derived frontage from North Andover public way). Final district placed at The Willows at Boxford (14.88 ac), which residents opposed as nearly undevelopable due to condo-law constraints.

City Council voted 6-2 on Dec 19 2023 (councilors O'Brien and Mackin Jr. dissented). Planning Board special meeting Nov 28 2023 voted 4-1 favorable (Grove dissented). Zoning created four multifamily overlay districts permitting ~3,769 units. EOHLC adoption date in seed (2023-12-14) predates the Dec 19 council vote — likely refers to an earlier submission or committee action; the decisive full council vote was Dec 19 2023. One of 12 rapid-transit communities meeting the year-end 2023 deadline.

Town Council voted 8-1 on April 30 2024 adopting a form-based code for the central business district to meet MBTA Communities requirements. EOHLC later (April 2025) found the district in only Conditional Compliance — district covered 610 units vs 1,401 required. A final compliance ordinance (D-FY26-001) was subsequently prepared. Planning board recommendation details not found in available sources. Seed EOHLC status is Compliant; actual compliance path involved a conditional phase and subsequent amendment.
